PullRequest.Title: agentHost: resolve relative links and show URL approval targets
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- Resolve relative response links against the chat's working directory, as images already are, in both live Agent Host sessions and recorded history.
- Include the target URL in pending URL approval prompts using metadata already received by the client. Preserve explicit UI presentation, markdown messages, and messages that already contain the URL.

The URL presentation is a temporary compatibility fallback. Its TODO assigns the final presentation to the host; the fallback can be removed once the host includes the target in its confirmation message. No protocol changes or permission-enforcement changes.

## How to test

In an Agent Host conversation, open a relative file link from a response, including after reopening history. Trigger a URL approval and verify the target is visible before approving.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed on the combined validation branch.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/metadataCompatibility.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/toolPresentation.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.test.ts` — 1080 passing in the original focused run; included again in the passing combined release suites.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed on the combined validation branch.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD -- "*.ts" | xargs npm run eslint --` — passed on the combined validation branch.

Not run: a live Agent Host end-to-end session or manual UI verification.

## Review follow-up

Review also found that an attached live provider could return a relative link unchanged and prevent the recorded-history resolver from running. The composite handler now falls back to recorded context in that case. `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionHandler.test.ts` - 59 passing after the correction, including failed live loading. The final combined release suite passed 2039 tests with 2 pre-existing pending; type, layer and lint checks passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render live Agent Host response Markdown containing relative and absolute links
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown rendering synchronously calls the session URI resolver once per link; the resolver reads in-memory session/chat state, derives the first working directory, parses URIs, and rewrites the target before the anchor can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of links in the rendered Markdown multiplied by the number of full/incremental Markdown renders while a response streams; links are not deduplicated because each anchor requires its own target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All resolution is synchronous and serialized on the UI rendering path; no queue, limiter, IPC, or asynchronous work is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session and chat snapshots are already held in maps/subscriptions. The working-directory string is parsed per resolver call rather than cached, but there is no cold remote lookup, cache miss, negative-cache behavior, or coalescing opportunity involving an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new base-directory lookup and URI parsing run per link, based on the Markdown transformUri call path into AgentHostSessionHandler; high confidence that the path remains entirely in memory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very link-heavy responses and repeated streaming renders increase small object/string/URI allocations, but realistic cardinality and duration are uncertain and existing Markdown parsing/DOM work dominates; the added work does not establish a concrete user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff extends existing image resolution to links with bounded synchronous CPU/allocation work and introduces no external boundary, collection scan, retained state, or asymptotic change beyond per-link processing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render recorded Cloud Sandbox history links before, during, or after live-provider attachment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Markdown link first consults the synchronous live resolver when present; if it returns the unchanged href, the composite synchronously consults the recorded in-memory context and rewrites the link before rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered links and response re-renders. For unchanged links, at most two in-memory resolver calls occur; effective cardinality remains one live attempt plus one recorded fallback per anchor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resolvers execute serially on the UI thread. No promise, worker, limiter, network request, filesystem read, or IPC call is started by URI resolution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recorded chat context and parsed working-directory URI are cached in a ResourceMap for the session lifetime and removed on session disposal. Live session state is already subscription-backed. There are no cold/warm boundary differences or repeated failed remote lookups.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the composite handler and read-only handler call path that fallback can add one in-memory rewrite and that no expensive boundary is transitively reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External and already-normalized links can take the extra recorded fallback when the live provider returns the original href, but both operations are bounded URI/string work; no evidence shows enough realistic links for measurable rendering degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fallback adds bounded per-link CPU work to preserve recorded context, with no fan-out, blocking I/O, unbounded allocation, or retained-resource growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Present a pending URL permission card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool-call presentation checks protocol metadata, validates the URL request, optionally checks whether the invocation text already contains the URL, and formats one display string before the confirmation UI renders.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of pending confirmation tool cards and presentation refreshes; the new URL-specific metadata work is status-gated and does not run past the initial status checks for streaming, running, or completed calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous per tool card with no parallelism, queue, or asynchronous operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or needed; metadata resides on the tool-call object, and each presentation derives a short-lived string/object. There are no boundary-backed cold or warm states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from readToolCallPresentation and readCopilotUrlPermissionPresentation that the work is status-gated, local, and bounded to one request/message.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: URL and invocation-message lengths control linear string scanning/formatting, but permission metadata is expected to be small and pending cards are low-cardinality; no unbounded protocol transformation or downstream large-data copy was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change performs only bounded metadata checks and string formatting for low-cardinality pending confirmations, without I/O, fan-out, or retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced live-link rendering, recorded/live Cloud Sandbox fallback, and URL-permission presentation. The diff adds only bounded in-memory URI/string work on existing render paths, with no expensive boundary calls, unbounded state, concurrency burst, or high-confidence user-visible performance regression.
